user.title: Synology router or access point
user.description: Connect to one SRM device. Add each router and access point on its own; their client lists are combined. Help: [documentation]({docs})

data_description.host: Address or host name of the router or access point.
data_description.port: Leave empty for SRM's default: 8001 for HTTPS, 8000 for HTTP.
data_description.verify_certificate: Pin the device's certificate after you confirmed its fingerprint. Turn off only if you accept that anyone in your network could read the password.

certificate.title: Confirm the certificate
certificate.description:
The device presents a certificate with this SHA-256 fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the certificate shown in SRM's settings. Continue only if it matches; Home Assistant then trusts exactly this certificate.

credentials.title: Administrator account
credentials.description: SRM's Web API only answers administrators. Help: [documentation]({docs})

data_description.username: An SRM administrator account without two-factor authentication; a dedicated account is best.

clients.title: Device trackers
clients.description: Choose the clients Home Assistant should track. You can change this later in the options.

data_description.track_all: Creates a tracker for every client, including new ones later.
data_description.tracked: Only these clients get a tracker. Leave empty for none.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: Home Assistant could not sign in to {host}. Enter the account again.

data_description.username: An SRM administrator account without two-factor authentication; a dedicated account is best.

reauth_certificate.title: New certificate
reauth_certificate.description:
The device now presents a different certificate:

`{fingerprint}`

This is expected after a certificate renewal. Compare it with SRM and continue only if it matches.

reconfigure_certificate.title: Confirm the certificate
reconfigure_certificate.description:
The device presents a different certificate than the one trusted so far:

`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the certificate shown in SRM's settings. Continue only if it matches; Home Assistant then trusts exactly this certificate.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Change how Home Assistant reaches this device.

data_description.host: Address or host name of the router or access point.
data_description.port: Leave empty for SRM's default: 8001 for HTTPS, 8000 for HTTP.
data_description.verify_certificate: Pin the device's certificate after you confirmed its fingerprint. Turn off only if you accept that anyone in your network could read the password.

error.cannot_connect: The device could not be reached.
error.invalid_auth: Wrong username or password, or the account may not log in.
error.two_factor: The account uses two-factor authentication. Use an account without it.
error.blocked: The device blocks logins from Home Assistant after failed attempts. Unblock the address in SRM's auto block settings, or wait until the block expires.
error.certificate: The certificate does not match. Check the address, then confirm the new fingerprint.
error.invalid_host: Enter a host name or an IP address, without port or path.
error.not_admin: The account is not an administrator. SRM's Web API only answers administrators.
error.no_serial: The device reports no serial number, so it cannot be set up.

abort.already_configured: This device is already set up.
abort.wrong_device: This is a different device than the one set up.

data_description.track_all: Creates a tracker for every client, including new ones later.
data_description.tracked: Only these clients get a tracker. Leave empty for none.
data_description.fast_interval: Clients, Wi-Fi, load and WAN. Default 30 s.

invalid_auth.message: Wrong username or password, or the account may not log in.

two_factor.message: The account uses two-factor authentication. Use an account without it.

certificate.message: The certificate does not match. Check the address, then confirm the new fingerprint.

not_admin.message: The account is not an administrator. SRM's Web API only answers administrators.

blocked.message: The device blocks logins from Home Assistant after failed attempts. Unblock the address in SRM's auto block settings, or wait until the block expires.

blocked.title: {name} blocks Home Assistant
blocked.description: SRM's auto block refuses logins from Home Assistant after failed attempts, so {name} is not read. Home Assistant tries to log in again every 15 minutes; each attempt counts towards the block. Unblock Home Assistant's address in SRM's auto block settings, or wait until the block expires. This message disappears after the next successful update.
